title: Lithium-6 enrichment supply chain for fusion
bottleneck: Tritium breeding depends on lithium-6, which makes up only 7.5 percent of natural lithium and must be enriched to 30 to 90 percent for efficient breeding blankets. Commercial lithium-6 enrichment capacity barely exists outside legacy weapons programs, and building it involves mercury-based processes regulators dislike or unproven laser and plasma methods. A single gigawatt plant needs 50 to 100 tonnes of enriched lithium-6 inventory.
why_it_blocks: Fusion could stall before it starts if the fuel precursor supply chain does not exist. Dozens of plants would need thousands of tonnes of enriched lithium-6, a market that today is essentially zero.
current_state: A few startups are developing plasma centrifuge and laser enrichment for lithium-6, and fusion companies are signing early supply MOUs, but no commercial-scale lithium-6 enrichment plant is operating.
